items.title: CONSENT CALENDAR

Award Contract Nos. PRO.0227(R2).A-D, As-Needed Power Operations Support Agreements, to Siemens Industry, Inc. (PRO.0227(R2).A), Utilicast, LLC (PRO.0227(R2).B), Clean Energy Capital Securities LLC (PRO.0227(R2).C), and Ascend Analytics (PRO.0227(R2).D), each for an amount not-to-exceed $2,000,000 and with a duration of five years, to provide specialized professional services for the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Power Enterprise

Approve Modification No. 1 to Job Order Contract No. JOC-89, General Engineering (A License) Construction, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, and Alameda Counties with Trinet Construction, Inc., to increase the contract duration by one year for a total contract duration of three years, allowing additional time to complete ongoing facility and asset improvements

REGULAR CALENDAR Adopt a refined Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act - Purchase and Sale Agreement and Easement Deed with Sunol Glen Unified School District
items.text: Adopt a refined Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act; Approve the terms and conditions and authorize the General Manager to execute a Purchase and Sale Agreement and Easement Deed with Sunol Glen Unified School District for the acquisition of a 4,008-square-foot easement for an underground water pipeline and associated appurtenances and a 34,834-square-foot temporary construction easement on and across a portion of Alameda County Assessor’s Parcel No. 096-0155-004-01, known as 11601 Main Street, Sunol, California, for $35,000, subject to Board of Supervisors’ and Mayor’s approval

items.title: Approve the expansion of the Wastewater, Water, and Power Enterprise Interim Funding Programs from $750 million, $500 million, and $250 million, to not-to-exceed aggregate principal amounts of $1.25 billion, $750 millio
items.text: Approve the expansion of the Wastewater, Water, and Power Enterprise Interim Funding Programs from $750 million, $500 million, and $250 million, to not-to-exceed aggregate principal amounts of $1.25 billion, $750 million, and $450 million, respectively; and authorize the General Manager, or the General Manager’s designee, to prepare and introduce an ordinance with the terms described here for adoption by the Board of Supervisors and approval by the Mayor

items.title: Accept work performed by Mitchell Engineering under Contract No. DB-129.1 Bay Corridor Transmission and Distribution – Phase 2 (2019) North; approve Modification No. 21 - decreasing the contract amount by $1,276,441 for
items.text: Accept work performed by Mitchell Engineering under Contract No. DB-129.1 Bay Corridor Transmission and Distribution – Phase 2 (2019) North; approve Modification No. 21 (Final) decreasing the contract amount by $1,276,441 for a total contract amount of $20,691,291 and increasing the contract duration by 696 consecutive calendar days for a total contract duration of 1,195 consecutive calendar days (approximately three years and three months), to cover a time impact analysis reconciliation for a compensable delay related to resequencing of duct bank work and dewatering for higher groundwater, final reconciliation of bid items and costs, and for contractor to complete closeout punch-list items, including resolution of Fluidized Thermal Backfill exceeding design strength, and preparation of as-built drawings and supporting documentation; and authorize final payment to the contractor

items.title: Accept work performed by Rubecon Builders, Inc., under Contract No. WD-2687R, Auxiliary Water Supply System Pumping Station No. 2 Improvements
items.text: Accept work performed by Rubecon Builders, Inc., under Contract No. WD-2687R, Auxiliary Water Supply System Pumping Station No. 2 Improvements (2016); approve Modification No. 14 (Final) increasing the contract amount by $1,111,992, within the approved contingency amount, for a total contract amount of $22,699,579, and increasing the contract duration by 817 consecutive calendar days for a total contract duration of 2,180 consecutive calendar days (approximately five years and 11 months), to resolve claims for additional compensation for time impacts and extended overhead, reconcile overall contract duration due to contractor- and owner-caused delays due to differing site conditions, electrical modifications, various improvements within the building due to existing conditions including additional painting, demolition, pipe and structural supports, utility repairs, concrete repairs, fire alarm system modifications), and complete administrative closeout; and authorize final payment to the contractor
